Definition: from G37; properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier:--holiness, sanctification.
BiblicalUsage: hagiasmós is a plain word for holiness, sanctification. In Romans 6:19, the text says "even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness." In 1 Corinthians 1:30, the text says "and sanctification."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hagiasmós matters because purity is not prudishness; it is keeping ourselves for the God who made us. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
